title: Implement level independent transient pick attack shaper
description:
Create Source/DSP/TransientShaper.h and Source/DSP/TransientShaper.cpp implementing a level-independent transient pick-attack shaper.

Implement a dual envelope follower with tau_fast=1ms and tau_slow=15ms (one-pole followers whose coefficients are computed from the sample rate in a prepare()/prepareToPlay-style setup). Compute the relative attack delta as delta_rel = clamp((e_fast - e_slow) / (e_slow + epsilon), 0.0, 2.0) so the effect is independent of absolute signal level. Apply a gain shaped by delta_rel scaled by the smoothed pick_attack amount to emphasize transients.

Binding real-time rules: no heap allocation, locks, file IO, or string construction inside the per-sample/processBlock path; instantiate juce::ScopedNoDenormals at the top of any block-processing method; allocate all state during prepare. Use linear juce::SmoothedValue for the pick_attack dB amount. Provide a class TransientShaper with prepare(double sampleRate, int maxBlockSize), reset(), and a processing method operating on a juce::dsp::AudioBlock or float buffers.

Before editing, inspect:
- CMakeLists.txt to see how Source/DSP module files are added to the target and the juce_add_plugin/target_link_libraries setup.
- Source/DSP/ for existing header/cpp conventions (namespace, include guards, prepare/reset signatures) from earlier phases.
- JUCE/modules/juce_dsp for juce::dsp::AudioBlock and juce::SmoothedValue usage (read only; do not modify anything under JUCE/).

STRICT FILE SCOPE: Create or modify ONLY the files listed in allowed_write_paths. Do not modify CMakeLists.txt in this task.
acceptance_criteria: Source/DSP/TransientShaper.h and Source/DSP/TransientShaper.cpp exist and declare/define a TransientShaper class with prepare, reset, and a process method
delta_rel is computed as clamp((e_fast - e_slow)/(e_slow + epsilon), 0.0, 2.0) with tau_fast=1ms and tau_slow=15ms
juce::ScopedNoDenormals is instantiated at the top of the block-processing method and no heap allocation occurs in the per-sample path
cmake --build build --target ShredBoost succeeds after these files are wired in (verified in the compose/verification tasks)
No file outside allowed_write_paths is created or modified
forbidden_changes: perform heap allocation, locking, or string construction inside the per-sample processing path

allowed: add private one-pole envelope follower helpers
